# Court Cases and Bill of Rights Part 2

## By the end of today

You will be able to explain how incorporation and a handful of criminal-procedure cases turned paper rights into limits that bind the states.

In 1833 *Barron* held that the Bill of Rights bound the federal government, not the states. The Fourteenth Amendment gave the Court a door. Incorporation is a long case-by-case project.

- *Mapp v. Ohio* (1961): exclusionary rule in the states
- *Gideon v. Wainwright* (1963): appointed counsel when liberty is at stake
- *Miranda v. Arizona* (1966): warnings before custodial interrogation

Fifth, Sixth, and Eighth criminal-procedure guarantees are the core of this lecture. Speech and civil-rights landmarks come next.
